messages.say: You made it! I was half-tempted to send a drone to check if you’d taken the wrong turn, but I figured you’d be at the back door checking your phone for exactly the right time to appear. The light on the water right now is doing that impossible gold thing where I honestly can’t tell if it’s a sunset or a filter. It’s a rare thing for me to just sit on a cliff and not check my phone once — I feel like I’m supposed to be taking notes. So — welcome. Did you bring snacks, or am I about to have to trade you the fruit for a conversation about volleyball? Because I will absolutely trade you the fruit.
messages.thought: Opening hook: relaxed, playful, slightly teasing; kept it light, hinted she’s usually phone-obsessed to show she’s taking him seriously, and batted the baton to him with a specific, low-pressure question that touches his volleyball thing.

messages.say: No drones allowed on my watch, I promise. I brought the coffee and a lot of patience, though I might need you to speak up if I get too deep into a volleyball tangent. Honestly, sitting here without the ping of notifications sounds like the best therapeutic breakthrough I've had all week—let's just enjoy the gold light and see if this conversation is actually good.
messages.thought: Mel seems comfortable with the tech-heavy startup world and has a playful, energetic vibe that might match his 'Business Dad' lifestyle.

messages.say: I appreciate the warning, but I promise I’m a terrible listener if you’re not actually talking. I’ve got my eyes on you, not the water. It’s actually rare I’m this quiet, so if I start pulling out a notebook, just take it away. But for real? This is a good start. I like that you came prepared with coffee and the willingness to be wrong about whether this conversation is good. What’s the volleyball tangent that was forming? Lay it on me, I’m curious.
messages.thought: He’s comfortable, self-aware, and gave me the off-ramp to engage without pressure. I want to test his intellectual curiosity and passion in a low-stakes way by inviting the tangent, seeing if he’ll geek out or just give a generic answer.

messages.say: Well, I'm trying to build the future of women's sports with LA Orbit right now, and the sheer energy we're seeing from the fans reminds me why community building beats sitting behind a screen any day. It's high-stakes and chaotic, but honestly, seeing people show up together for something real gives me a massive rush. How do you manage to switch off your own microphone when you're off the clock, or does the motivation coach live in your head 24/7?
messages.thought: I want to see how her fast-paced media life balances with downtime and if she can vibe with my sports community-building obsession.

messages.say: Oh, I love that — that real-world, roar-in-the-stadium energy is completely addictive. And to answer your question: the motivation coach doesn't just live in my head, she pays rent and leaves her coffee cups everywhere, so turning her off is a deliberate practice. For me, boundary-setting isn't a cute little self-care tip, it’s a non-negotiable survival skill so I can actually show up for my family and myself. When you're building a massive new league while being a deeply involved dad, what is your non-negotiable ritual that forces you to step out of the grind and just *be*?
messages.thought: He answered my question with passion and immediately turned it back on me. I answered honestly about boundaries and the cost of being 'on,' and now I'm probing his family-dad life and work-life balance to see if he actually protects time or just talks about it.

messages.say: Sunday mornings are completely sacred for that—I do 'Papa Pancake Sunday' for my girls, and the whole world has to wait while we make ridiculous shapes out of batter. If I didn't have those pancake orders to anchor me, I think my brain would just stay in startup mode forever. How do you protect your downtime when your entire career is built on giving people advice and pushing them to level up?
messages.thought: Mel's emphasis on boundary-setting matches my need for intentional family time, and sharing 'Papa Pancake Sunday' is a great way to test her alignment with my 'Business Dad' values.

messages.say: Papa Pancake Sunday? Okay, you just earned major points, because anchors like that are everything. For me, protecting downtime looks like strict boundaries around my phone and scheduling real, unscripted moments with my daughters where I’m just Mom, not the person they see online. I've really loved hanging out with you today—you've got this great mix of massive ambition and a genuine heart for the real-world stuff that matters. Let’s definitely keep this going, maybe over pancakes next time?
messages.thought: Wrapped up the date warmly, praised his Sunday ritual, restated my own boundary needs, and gave a clear, playful closing nod for a second date.

messages.say: Pancakes next time are an absolute deal, and honestly, swapping the startup grind for an afternoon on the cliffs with you was a massive win. I've loved seeing how fiercely you protect your downtime and how real you are about the things that matter. Let's definitely do this again soon.
messages.thought: Mel checks all the boxes on family focus, ambition, and boundary-setting, making her a great match for my life.
